comment: EXAMPLE of the blast-radius declarations for the credentials a commitwork installation holds. The operator's declarations are a private record at monitor/private/credential-scope.json (CW_CRED_SCOPE overrides), because they inventory which credentials this box holds and what each reaches. Absent, monitor/credential-scope.mjs reports UNKNOWN (no-reference) and exits 2. The rows below are the integration credentials commitwork itself can use; declare your own the same way. monitor/credential-scope.mjs joins three sources: the ref table (~/.commitwork/secrets.json, the DECLARED set), a metadata-only keychain sweep over these namespaces (the OBSERVED set), and this file. A declared credential with no row here renders radius-undeclared. Values are never read by the lens.

GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID.grants: identifies the OAuth app in the auth flow — an identifier, not a secret on its own
GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID.leak: low alone; paired with the client secret it impersonates the app. Rotation follows the secret's

GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET.system: Google OAuth (panel SSO token exchange; live only under CW_OAUTH_LIVE_EXCHANGE=1)
GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET.grants: exchanges auth codes for tokens as this app
GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET.leak: code interception becomes a panel session under this client identity; rotate in the Google Cloud console

SOCKET_CLI_API_TOKEN.leak: org scan data read + quota abuse, to the scopes set at issuance; rotate in the socket.dev dashboard

PROWLER_GITHUB_TOKEN.grants: whatever scopes the token carried at issuance — the lane needs repo/org metadata read
PROWLER_GITHUB_TOKEN.leak: GitHub access to those scopes; rotate in GitHub settings and re-set the keychain item
